subject: geography
title: Coastal Management Strategies
welcome_lead: Compare hard and soft engineering with sustainable approaches.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on hard, soft and managed realignment coastal strategies.
final_note: ICZM integrates physical, economic and social priorities.

concepts.def: Structural defences: sea walls, groynes, rock armour, gabions.
Working with nature: beach nourishment, dune regeneration, marsh creation.
Allowing the sea to flood land previously defended, creating new habitat.
Integrated Coastal Zone Management; holistic stakeholder approach.
Identifies policy: hold the line, advance, no active intervention, managed realignment.
Evaluation comparing defence costs with assets protected.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sea wall at Sea Palling, Norfolk, cost £14 million in 1997. Reflective walls can scour beach. Groynes at Mappleton cost £2 million but caused downdrift erosion at Cowden. Rip-rap is cheaper but visually intrusive.

Beach nourishment at Bournemouth pumped 1.5 million m^3 sand at cost £8 million; widely seen as cost-effective. Dune regeneration at Studland Bay uses marram grass planting. Soft approaches work with natural processes and avoid downdrift damage.

Medmerry (2013) breached sea wall to create 183 hectares of intertidal habitat, protecting 348 homes. Cost £28 million; saved estimated £90 million over 100 years. Created saltmarsh habitat for wildlife and absorbs storm energy.
